plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MU, METU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, holding a substantial cash buffer for stability. Drawdowns are expected to be minimal.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to minimal levels.
Maintain SPY at 25% for broad market exposure.
Add to METU and CRWD to increase AI/Software exposure.
Initiate a new position in NET, a top scanner setup.
This plan balances growth with risk management.
Targeting a moderate ~2.5% monthly return with controlled risk.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly return by blending broad index exposure with quality tech and limited leverage. It trims high-risk leveraged ETFs while adding to strong performers and new opportunities. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to free up capital for concentrated bets.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs SOXL, MUU, and METU.
Significantly increase CRWD to 15% for AI concentration.
Initiate a new position in NET, a top scanner setup.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly return by leaning into leverage and concentration, especially in semiconductors and AI. It increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and top-rated single names, accepting higher risk for potentially greater reward. Be aware of amplified drawdowns and leveraged ETF decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MU, METU) and high-beta single names (CRWD, SNOW).
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce volatility and increase cash buffer.
Significantly increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and capital preservation.
Expect low volatility and reliable, though variable, income distributions.
This is not a savings account; NAV can still decline.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing stability and cash flow. It eliminates leverage and high-beta single names, focusing on income-generating ETFs like QQQI and a reduced broad index position. Drawdowns are expected to be minimal, but growth potential is also limited.
